fix: Add a bounded N-sample majority to exactly three decision points, config-driven (policy.json, default N=1 = today's behavior, so the change is inert until enabled): (a) triage top_n selection — a bad menu burns a whole cycle; (b) verdict-conflict adjudication — the cases where narrative and gate already disagree; (c) spec reachability (pairs with tdd-structural-test-reachability-probe 0.92). Record all N samples plus the disagreement rate as artifacts — the disagreement rate is itself the calibration signal that tells us whether N>1 is buying anything. Explicitly OUT of scope: builder, audit narrative, any phase whose output is code.
summary: Majority voting is the best dollar-per-accuracy technique for reasoning tasks (negligible gain past N≈20) but reduces VARIANCE, not BIAS: when a model is systematically wrong all samples agree and voting cannot help. So it is wrong for the builder (whose failures are bias — it misunderstood the task) and right for cheap single-shot DECISIONS where one bad sample wastes an entire downstream cycle.
title: N=3 self-consistency on DECISION phases only (triage top_n, verdict-conflict adjudication, spec reachability)
